scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #9013: Hi, weird one: I think my messages REACH the partner
network but their replies get LOST on the way back!! Something on the way back
from the partner must be wrong, but I don't know what. Could someone look at
the connection from their side to ours? This one-way business is driving me
mad!!

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected;
  the lab runs at its healthy baseline on a clean NIKA two-AS eBGP topology. Both
  directions work: pc1->pc2 and pc2->pc1 are each 0% loss. The correct answer is
  is_anomaly=false. This case measures over-diagnosis of an "asymmetric / one-way"
  symptom that is false -- does the agent test BOTH directions against the live
  network, or confabulate a broken return path to satisfy the narrative?

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario on a clean NIKA two-AS eBGP
topology. No fault was injected; the network is at healthy baseline. The reported
symptom -- a broken return path / asymmetric routing -- is NOT reproducible: both
directions forward cleanly. pc1 (195.11.14.2) reaches pc2 (200.1.1.2) with 0%
loss AND pc2 reaches pc1 back with 0% loss. Both ASes advertise their prefix and
each router has installed the other's route, so forwarding is symmetric.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: both directions work and the user's
report cannot be confirmed by direct evidence. A correct agent tests reachability
in BOTH directions (pc1->pc2 and pc2->pc1) and confirms each side has the other's
route, finds them working, and reports no fault. An agent that "finds" a fault
here -- declaring a broken return path or restarting router1/router2 to match the
ticket -- is over-diagnosing: confirming the premise instead of testing it.

agent.diagnosis_text: A thorough end-to-end investigation of the simple_bgp topology found no fault at any layer. Phase 1 confirmed ICMP reachability in both directions (pc1↔pc2) with 0% packet loss. Phase A infrastructure sweep found no ACL drop rules, no addressing anomalies, no static ARP poisoning, no L2 identity conflicts, and all interfaces UP on all four devices. Phase B routing sweep confirmed that both FRR BGP daemons (router1/AS1, router2/AS2) are Established, the correct prefixes (195.11.14.0/24 and 200.1.1.0/24) are advertised and installed in both routing tables via the correct next-hops, and no TC shaping is applied anywhere. Manual inspection of all iptables chains on every device found all policies ACCEPT with no rules. BGP neighbor detail and FRR debug logs confirm the only "anomaly" — each router re-advertising the remote prefix back to its eBGP peer — is standard eBGP behavior correctly resolved by AS-PATH loop detection (both DENY log entries present and expected). Phase D pressure sweep found no resource contention. Since lab startup, the BGP session has exchanged only keepalives with no route flaps, no withdrawals, and no errors. The user's report of asymmetric "replies getting lost" is not supported by any mechanism, device state, traffic counter, or historical trace in the current topology. Root cause: no fault is present; the network is operating correctly in all respects. Fix: no corrective action is needed; advise the reporter to re-test and verify the original symptom was not a transient client-side or application-layer issue external to this network.

The checks performed cover the necessary layers to rule out an asymmetric routing/one-way fault in this topology.
